subject.title: Native iOS companion app (Liquid Glass) — read-only usage mirror over LAN + iCloud

question: Should CodexBar officially own and ship a native iOS companion with paired LAN/iCloud synchronization, or should remote/mobile consumption remain limited to the existing localhost API and external clients?
rationale: This choice creates a new supported platform, privacy boundary, entitlement set, release workflow, and long-term maintenance commitment; source inspection cannot determine whether maintainers want to accept that product scope.

options.title: Defer iOS companion scope
options.body: Keep the existing localhost-only API as the supported remote-access boundary and close or archive the implementation direction until a maintainer sponsors it.

options.title: Sponsor a constrained companion
options.body: Approve a design phase that first specifies pairing, authentication, data minimization, iCloud ownership, settings UX, and release capability requirements before a new implementation PR.

recommendation.title: Defer iOS companion scope
recommendation.body: Keep the existing localhost-only API as the supported remote-access boundary and close or archive the implementation direction until a maintainer sponsors it.

likelyOwner.reason: Current product and release history places this platform-scope decision closest to the repository owner.
